items.reason: Pinning a tag to a SHA means asking GitHub what the tag points at right now, and this session has no network; the repository already ships the one networked command that closes it (`npm run actions:pin`, which rewrites the workflows AND flips STRICT/RATCHET in the same pass), so inventing SHAs or adding another burn-down job would be worse than leaving it.

The half that is still open is history — measuring and re-attributing past subjects needs git, which this session cannot run; the forward half is already fenced (rubric A5 blocks via review:agent:gate inside check:ci and the pre-push hook, with a known-bad fixture in test-unit/gate-bite.test.mjs, and scripts/commit-attribution.mjs writes the authorship and provenance trailers from the commit hooks).

Already closed before this cycle: .github/guidance-budget.json declares the seven read-first documents with a line ceiling on each and on the total, scripts/guidance-budget.mjs measures it, and test-unit/guidance-budget.test.mjs blocks on every build — this session paid the ceiling honestly (126 → 127 for docs/task-index.md) rather than editing around it.

Already closed before this cycle: scripts/lib/review-prompt.mjs fences every untrusted surface with a per-run nonce, test-llm/injection/corpus.json holds the hostile cases for both model surfaces (the review and the issue dispatch), test-unit/prompt-injection.test.mjs blocks on containment with an unfenced negative control, and the live refusal drill runs weekly in llm-drift.yml.

Every credential flow in docs/security/threat-model.md now carries a TM-nn id, fourteen of the fifteen are claimed by the suite that asserts the fence the row names, and test-unit/threat-flows.test.mjs blocks when a flow is unclaimed, a citation rots, or a cited path has moved.

Staged exposure is a deployment-platform change (Vercel skew/aliases or a flag SDK) plus a halt signal nobody has agreed on; AGENTS.md puts anything that changes what production runs on the operator's side, and there is nothing offline in this repository that would make a canary real rather than declared.

scripts/guidance-commands.mjs resolves every `npm run …` quoted in the read-first set, the documents task-index routes to and the five entry points against package.json, blocking through test-unit/guidance-commands.test.mjs, and reports the scripts no guidance names.

Already closed before this cycle: test-unit/gate-bite.test.mjs gives every stage of check:ci a known-bad fixture, a delegated suite or a written exemption, and the COVERAGE list is held closed against the CHAIN in scripts/gate-remedy.mjs, so a gate added to the chain without a proof that it bites turns the unit suite red.

lessons: This repository's gates are mostly cheap file-reading checks wired through test-unit/*.test.mjs rather than as new check:ci stages — adding a stage drags in a gate-remedy entry, a gate-bite fixture row, a constraint-map rule and a timing baseline, so a new fence is cheapest and most conventional as a unit test that spawns its own script.

Ascent findings here can be several cycles stale: four of the eight items named gaps that prior work had already closed (the injection corpus, the gate-bite fixtures, the guidance budget). Read the tree before writing anything — the honest answer for those is a skip that names the existing artefact, not a second implementation of it.

Anything added to AGENTS.md or docs/task-index.md is priced: .github/guidance-budget.json pins both at their exact current line count, so a paragraph costs a ceiling raise with a written reason. Routing a new tool from the task index (one line) rather than describing it in the canonical document (seven) is the move the budget's own $howToChange asks for.
